Storing Mass Spectrometry Data in MongoDB Databases

Source: vignettes/MsBackendMongoDb.Rmd
MsBackendMongoDb.Rmd

Introduction

The Spectra Bioconductor package provides a flexible and expandable infrastructure for handling and processing mass spectrometry (MS) data in R. The package supports interchangeable use of different backends that provide additional file format support or different ways to store and represent MS data. The MsBackendMongoDb package expands Spectra enabling to store and retrieve MS data from MongoDB databases. MongoDB is a NoSQL database for storing structured, semi-structured and unstructured data.

Installation and system requirements

MsBackendMongoDb along with all required dependencies can be installed with:

install.packages("BiocManager")
install.packages("remotes")
BiocManager::install("RforMassSpectrometry/MsBackendMongoDb")

For using MsBackendMongoDb, access to a MongoDB, either running locally or remotely, is required. See the official MongoDB web page for information on installation and setup of a MongoDB database server.

Storing MS data in a MongoDB database

In this section we store MS data from two mzML files into an empty MongoDB database. We create below a Spectra object representing the MS data from these two data files.

library(Spectra)
## Loading required package: S4Vectors
## Loading required package: stats4
## Loading required package: BiocGenerics
## Loading required package: generics
## 
## Attaching package: 'generics'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
##     setequal, union
## 
## Attaching package: 'BiocGenerics'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     IQR, mad, sd, var, xtabs
## The following object is masked from 'package:utils':
## 
##     data
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     anyDuplicated, aperm, append, as.data.frame, basename, cbind,
##     colnames, dirname, do.call, duplicated, eval, evalq, Filter, Find,
##     get, grep, grepl, is.unsorted, lapply, Map, mapply, match, mget,
##     order, paste, pmax, pmax.int, pmin, pmin.int, Position, rank,
##     rbind, Reduce, rownames, sapply, saveRDS, scale, sequence, table,
##     tapply, transform, unique, unsplit, which.max, which.min
## 
## Attaching package: 'S4Vectors'
## The following object is masked from 'package:utils':
## 
##     findMatches
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     expand.grid, I, unname
## Loading required package: BiocParallel
library(msdata)
## 
##  IMPORTANT: msdata will be deprecated and replaced by the new
##  MsDataHub package -- see https://bioconductor.org/packages/MsDataHub.
##  Please open an issue at https://github.com/rformassspectrometry/MsDataHub/issues
##  to inform us of any data from msdata that would need to be moved to MsDataHub.
fls <- dir(system.file("sciex", package = "msdata"), full.names = TRUE)

sp <- Spectra(fls)
sp
## MSn data (Spectra) with 1862 spectra in a MsBackendMzR backend:
##        msLevel     rtime scanIndex
##      <integer> <numeric> <integer>
## 1            1     0.280         1
## 2            1     0.559         2
## 3            1     0.838         3
## 4            1     1.117         4
## 5            1     1.396         5
## ...        ...       ...       ...
## 1858         1   258.636       927
## 1859         1   258.915       928
## 1860         1   259.194       929
## 1861         1   259.473       930
## 1862         1   259.752       931
##  ... 34 more variables/columns.
## 
## file(s):
## 20171016_POOL_POS_1_105-134.mzML
## 20171016_POOL_POS_3_105-134.mzML

This Spectra object has thus 1862 spectra. We next change the MS data storage mode for this object to a MongoDB database. We therefore establish below a connection to a local MongoDB server. The connectMsBackendMongoDb() function connects to a database with the name specified with parameter db and creates the required MongoDB collections to store the MS data. The database will be created automatically if it does not already exist. By setting parameter clean = TRUE we ensure that any previous database with the same name as defined with db gets first erased. Thus, this parameter should be used with caution!

#' connect to a MongoDB database
library(MsBackendMongoDb)
mcon <- connectMsBackendMongoDb(
    db = "ms_backend_mongodb",
    url = "mongodb://localhost:27017",
    clean = TRUE)

We can next use the setBackend() function to transfer the data from the original mzML files to the MongoDB database.

sp_mng <- setBackend(sp, backend = MsBackendMongoDb(), dbcon = mcon)

The memory requirements for a Spectra object with a MsBackendMongoDb are very low since only the IDs of the spectra are kept in the main memory while all data is stored in the database:

print(object.size(sp_mng), units = "MB")
## 0.3 Mb

Due to the design of the Spectra class, data can be retrieved irrespectively of where or how the data is stored. For Spectra objects using the MsBackendMongoDb backend, the data is extracted on-the-fly from the MongoDB database. Below we get the retention time values from the object and show the first 6 values.

rtime(sp_mng) |>
    head()
## [1] 0.280 0.559 0.838 1.117 1.396 1.675

Similarly, we can extract the m/z values of all spectra from the data set. Also in this case, the data is extracted from the database.

mz(sp_mng)
## NumericList of length 1862
## [["SP0001"]] 105.043454833354 105.044900379521 ... 133.983660012089
## [["SP0002"]] 105.027517517902 105.028962955892 ... 133.98364971537
## [["SP0003"]] 105.037635723077 105.03908123069 ... 133.990180037683
## [["SP0004"]] 105.037635723077 105.03908123069 ... 133.985282281029
## [["SP0005"]] 105.034744757582 105.036190245303 ... 133.988547442185
## [["SP0006"]] 105.041972245917 105.043417783368 ... 133.98364971537
## [["SP0007"]] 105.037635723077 105.03908123069 ... 133.998343164363
## [["SP0008"]] 105.034744757582 105.036190245303 ... 133.982017159657
## [["SP0009"]] 105.040526728357 105.041972255863 ... 133.980384613891
## [["SP0010"]] 105.036190235357 105.037635733023 ... 133.986914856634
## ...
## <1852 more elements>

Subset operations will only subset the spectra IDs in the backend, but not affect the data stored in the MongoDB. Below we subset the Spectra object to spectra with index 13, 5, 20 and 21:

sp_mng <- sp_mng[c(13, 5, 20, 21)]
sp_mng
## MSn data (Spectra) with 4 spectra in a MsBackendMongoDb backend:
##     msLevel precursorMz  polarity
##   <integer>   <numeric> <integer>
## 1         1          NA         1
## 2         1          NA         1
## 3         1          NA         1
## 4         1          NA         1
##  ... 35 more variables/columns.
##  Use  'spectraVariables' to list all of them.
## MongoDb collections:  ms_spectrum_coll, ms_peaks_coll 
## Processing:
##  Switch backend from MsBackendMzR to MsBackendMongoDb [Thu Jul  2 13:17:23 2026]

Any operation on this subset Spectra object will only retrieve data from the 4 selected spectra.

rtime(sp_mng)
## [1] 3.628 1.396 5.581 5.860

As mentioned above, the MongoDB database still contains the full data. We can thus use the reset() function to restore the Spectra object to its original state:

sp_mng <- reset(sp_mng)
sp_mng
## MSn data (Spectra) with 1862 spectra in a MsBackendMongoDb backend:
##        msLevel precursorMz  polarity
##      <integer>   <numeric> <integer>
## 1            1          NA         1
## 2            1          NA         1
## 3            1          NA         1
## 4            1          NA         1
## 5            1          NA         1
## ...        ...         ...       ...
## 1858         1          NA         1
## 1859         1          NA         1
## 1860         1          NA         1
## 1861         1          NA         1
## 1862         1          NA         1
##  ... 36 more variables/columns.
##  Use  'spectraVariables' to list all of them.
## MongoDb collections:  ms_spectrum_coll, ms_peaks_coll 
## Processing:
##  Switch backend from MsBackendMzR to MsBackendMongoDb [Thu Jul  2 13:17:23 2026]
##  Reset object. [Thu Jul  2 13:17:26 2026]

Finally, the data available from the Spectra object using the MsBackendMongoDb is identical to the original Spectra object with the data from the original mzML files. We compare below the retention times reported by both Spectra objects.

all.equal(rtime(sp), rtime(sp_mng))
## [1] TRUE

Also the m/z values are identical - with the exception of the names of the returned list.

all.equal(mz(sp), unname(mz(sp_mng)))
## [1] TRUE
